clue.text: Stop being active having run off during fight

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time, here the letters, of the other

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of run are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stops working after fleeing in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns RUN into URN, and 'during' sets URN inside BOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn out is to exhaust oneself and cease functioning, a phrasal verb for stopping activity.

clue.text: Try to finish always as you might say

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: finish is END and always is EVER, said together

explanation.surface: Someone aims to complete a task for good, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour as a verb is a formal synonym for attempt or try.

clue.text: After its use the written word is lost

definitions.text: After its use the written word is lost

parts.words: After its use the written word is lost
parts.note: describes a stationery tool that rubs pencil marks off the page

explanation.surface: A lament that writing disappears once a certain thing is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber removes pencil writing, so once applied the words vanish.

clue.text: Cable spring to go first

parts.note: to spring is to jump
to lead is to go in front

explanation.surface: A cable leaps forward to take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Jump leads (US jumper cables) connect a flat car battery to a charged one.
explanation.definitionFit: Jump leads are a pair of cables used to start a car with a dead battery.

clue.text: What authors use to make connections?

definitions.text: What authors use to make connections?

parts.words: What authors use to make connections?
parts.note: the style of handwriting in which letters are linked together

explanation.surface: A question about how writers network.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursive script links letters, so writers using it literally make connections on the page.

clue.text: Doctor accepting old note that's poor to middling

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A doctor takes on a past musical note and judges it unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is of only ordinary, rather poor quality.

clue.text: Elizabeth welcoming second time by composer

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth greets someone for a second time near a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Accuse bishop struggling again outside

indicators.note: outside says these letters wrap around the other piece
struggling suggests disorder, so the letters of again are rearranged

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Charging a bishop who is having another hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges AGAIN to A..AIGN, which 'outside' wraps around RR.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally charge someone in court, so to accuse.

clue.text: Artist who's on the lathe?

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ... was an English painter
a woodworker who shapes material on a lathe

explanation.surface: Asks whether a painter worked at a lathe.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the painter matches the trade word for a lathe operator.

clue.text: Craft seen in River Test

parts.note: the Indus is a major river of South Asia
to test something is to try it

explanation.surface: A boat spotted on the River Test, a Hampshire chalk stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Test' looks like the English trout river; split it into River and Test.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft can mean a trade or branch of business, as does industry.

clue.text: I name individual actually present

parts.note: an individual is a person

explanation.surface: Someone names a person who is really there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being there in person means being physically present, not by proxy.

clue.text: Not in suitable gear

parts.note: not in is out
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone is not wearing the right clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes, and gear is informal for clothing.

clue.text: Shook from question I have read aloud

parts.note: contracted to I've

indicators.note: aloud says the past tense of read is heard, not spelt

parts.note: past-tense read is pronounced like the colour

explanation.surface: Someone trembled after reciting a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aloud' applies only to 'read', which in the past tense is said RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Quivered is a past-tense verb meaning trembled or shook.

clue.text: Stripping one male across the Channel? Terribly boring!

parts.note: un is the masculine form of one in French, spoken across the English Channel

indicators.note: terribly suggests something messed up, so the letters of boring are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman taking his clothes off is deemed dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrobing is taking off robes, so undressing or stripping.

clue.text: Bottom line included relapse

indicators.note: included means placed within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: backside is a colloquial word for bottom

explanation.surface: A footnote included a mention of falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to slip back into bad habits, a relapse.

clue.text: One making third score removed this exit

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are shifted from their places, so this exit is rearranged

explanation.surface: A third goal was scored and someone walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so the third score reaches sixty.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal that brings a count to three twenties, i.e. sixty.

clue.text: General survey on the scene

parts.note: over can mean on or above
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A broad study being made on location.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a general summary or broad look at something.

clue.text: Being foxy, liven up dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so liven up is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looking alluring livens up the dancefloor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxy' suggests sexy, but here it means like a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulpine is the adjective for things relating to or resembling foxes.

clue.text: One French drink perhaps that's out of the ordinary

parts.note: un is French for one
a regular at a pub orders 'the usual', their customary drink

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's drink that is somehow strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual means uncommon or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Scolding from Rex after son leaves puzzle

indicators.note: after places the king piece behind the other
leaves means departs, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle
Rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone tells off Rex once their son abandons a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S out of REBUS to give REBU.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuking means reprimanding sharply, a synonym of scolding.

clue.text: Grow into suit

definitions.meaning: to develop and turn into something
to look good on, as a dress flatters someone

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to develop into and to flatter or look right on.

clue.text: 150 with nothing put in small room

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
O looks like zero
to set something is to put it in place

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty items with nothing installed in a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small room or cupboard for storage.

clue.text: Kid singing to open TV show

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: prog is short for a television programme

explanation.surface: A child sings to begin a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child, as kid is.

clue.text: Remarkable slick hit that's difficult to deal with

indicators.note: remarkable can be read as re-marked, so slick hit is rearranged

explanation.surface: An impressive smooth strike that is hard to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticklish situation is a delicate one requiring careful handling.

clue.text: Benjamin and Diana touring country

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana
Israel is a country

explanation.surface: Benjamin and Diana travel around a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli's first name was Benjamin, so the forename indicates the statesman.

clue.text: Centre route that's half the distance

parts.note: mid means centre
a way is a route

explanation.surface: A central path covering half a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Midway is the point halfway along a distance.

clue.text: Animal, pig, behind row of shrubs

indicators.note: behind places the pig piece after the other

parts.note: a hedge is a row of bushes
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A pig is found behind a line of bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgehog is a small spiny mammal, an example of an animal.
